questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-127
questions.question: If an approaching train is near enough or going fast enough to be a danger, you must:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution
Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed
Cross the tracks at your own risk
Find an alternative route across tracks

questions.answer_text: Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-118
questions.question: When driving at night, it is most important for you to:

options.text: Use your high beams at all times
Drive within range of your headlights
Be ready to brake more quickly
Watch for cars at intersections

questions.answer_text: Drive within range of your headlights

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-117
questions.question: If you drive past your exit on an expressway, you should:

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder, then back up to the exit
Drive to the next exit and leave the expressway
Make a U-turn at the nearest emergency turn area
Make a U-turn at the next service area

questions.answer_text: Drive to the next exit and leave the expressway

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-121
questions.question: Your car starts to skid on a slippery road. You should:

options.text: Brake quickly and keep the wheel straight
Lock your brakes until you have come to a complete stop
Steer in the direction you want the front wheels to go
Steer toward the side of the road to get off the wet pavement

questions.answer_text: Steer in the direction you want the front wheels to go

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-114
questions.question: When attempting to stop on a slippery road, the best action to take is:

options.text: Apply the brakes quickly and firmly
Apply the brakes in slow, steady strokes
Shift to a lower gear, do not use the brakes
Shift into neutral, do not use the brakes

questions.answer_text: Apply the brakes in slow, steady strokes

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-113
questions.question: When your right wheels run onto a soft shoulder, what is the best way to get back on the highway?

options.text: Apply the brakes firmly and steer gently to the left
Ease your foot off the gas and brake gently
Steer hard to the left and then gently to the right
Apply the brakes firmly and stop completely

questions.answer_text: Ease your foot off the gas and brake gently

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-122
questions.question: You have just left an expressway and are starting to drive on an ordinary highway. You should:

options.text: Check your tires for correct pressure
Check your speedometer to keep at the lower speed limit
Stay twice as far behind other cars
Change gradually to the lower speed limit

questions.answer_text: Check your speedometer to keep at the lower speed limit

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-120
questions.question: Expressways have "expressway entrance lanes" (acceleration lanes) so that drivers can:

options.text: Test their brakes before driving at expressway speeds
Stop at the end to wait for a traffic opening
Reach the proper speed before blending with traffic
Test the pickup of their cars

questions.answer_text: Reach the proper speed before blending with traffic

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-111
questions.question: When you drive at night, you can reduce the problem of glare from the headlights of an approaching car by:

options.text: Looking to the lower right side of your lane
Having the inside lights on to make the amount of light equal
Looking at the spot on the lower edge of the steering wheel
Wearing glasses with lightly tinted lenses

questions.answer_text: Looking to the lower right side of your lane

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-131
questions.question: This sign (railroad crossing) is a warning that you are approaching:

options.text: An intersection
A crosswalk
A railroad crossing
A blasting zone

questions.answer_text: A railroad crossing

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-130
questions.question: What vehicles must stop at all railroad crossings?

options.text: Pickup trucks
School buses and passenger buses carrying passengers
Motorcycles
Vehicles towing a trailer

questions.answer_text: School buses and passenger buses carrying passengers

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-124
questions.question: Night driving is dangerous because:

options.text: Some traffic signs are less visible at night
More vehicles are on the road at night
The distance we can see ahead is reduced
Street lights tend to blur our vision

questions.answer_text: The distance we can see ahead is reduced

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-115
questions.question: If a tire blows out, the proper thing to do is:

options.text: Speed up to gain traction and then pull to the right
Hold the steering wheel firmly, and ease up on the gas
Apply the brakes, then shift into neutral
Shift into neutral, then apply the brakes

questions.answer_text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, and ease up on the gas

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-123
questions.question: Which of the following statements applies to all driving emergency situations?

options.text: Always slow down gradually
Your first reaction is the best reaction
Think before you act
Apply your brakes immediately

questions.answer_text: Think before you act

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-119
questions.question: When you drive in heavy fog during daylight hours you should drive with your:

options.text: Headlights off
Parking lights on
Headlights on low beam
Headlights on high beam

questions.answer_text: Headlights on low beam

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-129
questions.question: What is the appropriate action to take when approaching a railroad crossing that does not have signals (such as lights or crossing gates)?

options.text: Always bring the car to a complete stop
Slow down and be prepared to stop
Do nothing; all railroad crosings have signals
Increase speed to get across the tracks quickly

questions.answer_text: Slow down and be prepared to stop

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-116
questions.question: When you get ready to leave an expressway, you should begin to use your turn signal:

options.text: Just as you get to the exit ramp
50 feet before the exit ramp
100 feet before the exit ramp
When you see cars behind you in the exit lane

questions.answer_text: 100 feet before the exit ramp

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-128
questions.question: If traffic prevents you from crossing all the way across a set of railroad tracks, you may proceed only when:

options.text: An approaching train is not moving fast enough to be a danger
There is room for your vehicle on the other side
At least one half of your vehicle can cross the tracks
No trains are in sight

questions.answer_text: There is room for your vehicle on the other side

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-125
questions.question: Why is driving on an expressway different from driving on an ordinary street?

options.text: You must think faster and handle your vehicle more effectively
Trucks have to go slower on the expressways
There is more of a tendency to exceed the speed limit
There is more of a tendency to "tailgate"

questions.answer_text: You must think faster and handle your vehicle more effectively

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-110
questions.question: You are getting on a highway which has a very short entrance lane. The safest way for you to enter the flow of traffic would be to:

options.text: Use as much ramp as possible to get up to cruising speed
Use the left lane of the highway to get up to cruising speed
Wait for a large gap in traffic then speed up quickly
Get up to cruising speed gradually so other cars will see you

questions.answer_text: Wait for a large gap in traffic then speed up quickly

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-126
questions.question: You may drive around or under a gate that is being lowered or raised at a railroad crossing:

options.text: As long as an approaching train is not too close
If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate
If you first look carefully in both directions
Under no circumstances

questions.answer_text: Under no circumstances

questions.name: sgE-7355144-1-112
questions.question: If your brake pedal suddenly sinks to the floor, you should first:

options.text: Try to pump it to build up the pressure
Shift into neutral and shut the engine off
Try to raise it by hooking your toe under it
Apply the parking brake hard to stop the car

questions.answer_text: Try to pump it to build up the pressure
